messages.content: Mpa umwandiko mugufi ku guteka ukoresheje ijambo "gushya" mu buryo bubiri, hanyuma umbaze ibibazo.

Umwandiko: Ku wa Gatandatu, Aline yatangiye guteka ibishyimbo saa kumi n'imwe z'umugoroba. Yabicaniriye buhoro kugira ngo bishye neza. Inkwi zari zumye, bityo zirashya vuba. Ibishyimbo bimaze gushya, Aline yabikuye ku ziko.

Ibibazo: Aline yatangiye guteka ryari? "Gushya" bisobanura iki ku bishyimbo no ku nkwi?
Yatangiye saa kumi n'imwe z'umugoroba. Ku bishyimbo, gushya ni ugukongoka; ku nkwi ni ukugurumana. Ese yashyizemo umunyu?

Igihe wavuze kirahuye n'umwandiko. Ku nkwi, "gushya" ni ukugurumana, nk'uko wabivuze. Ariko ku bishyimbo, "gushya" hano ni ugutekwa bikagera igihe cyo kuribwa, si ugukongoka. Umwandiko ntuvuga niba Aline yarashyizemo umunyu, bityo ntitwabihimba.

messages.content: How do I say “It is new” in Kinyarwanda? I use it in my morning routine.
Which thing is new? The Kinyarwanda form depends on the noun. Uravuga ishati, inkweto, cyangwa ikindi kintu?
I mean the shirt I wear to work.
Ishati nambara ku kazi ni nshya. This means “The shirt I wear to work is new.” With plural shirts, the agreement changes: Amashati nambara ku kazi ni mashya.

messages.content: How do I distinguish "We plan to cook beans" from "We will cook beans"? I also want to say that we changed the plan and will cook rice.

Use "Turateganya guteka ibishyimbo" for "We plan to cook beans." The planning is the main idea. Use "Tuzateka ibishyimbo" for "We will cook beans," where the future action is central. For the revision, say: "Twari twateganyije guteka ibishyimbo, ariko ubu tuzateka umuceri." This contrasts the earlier plan with the new future action.

messages.content: Ndashaka kuvuga nti: "Mbere na mbere nasuye neighborhood, then ndeba inzu iri hafi y'isoko." Nabivuga nte mu Kinyarwanda gusa?
Wavuga uti: "Mbere na mbere nasuye ako gace, hanyuma ndeba inzu iri hafi y'isoko." Aha "ako gace" ni ko gasimbura neighborhood, naho "hanyuma" igasimbura then kandi igahuza ibikorwa uko bikurikirana.
Iyo nzu narayikunze, ariko nashakaga no kuvuga ko nyuma nabajije niba ako gace gatekanye nijoro.
Wakomeza uti: "Iyo nzu narayikunze, ariko nyuma nabajije niba ako gace gatekanye nijoro." "Iyo nzu" yerekeza ku nzu wavuze iri hafi y'isoko, naho "ako gace" kagumya kwerekeza ku gace wasuye.
Noneho mpa interuro imwe ikurikiranya ibyo byose, ariko ntuvuge ko inzu ari iyanjye.
"Mbere na mbere nasuye ako gace, hanyuma ndeba inzu iri hafi y'isoko; narayikunze, ariko nyuma mbaza niba ako gace gatekanye nijoro." Interuro ivuga ko wakunze inzu, ariko ntivuga ko ari iyawe.

messages.content: How do I change “Mpa inkuru yawe” from informal to formal when speaking to one storyteller?

Informal: Mpa inkuru yawe.
Polite: Mwampa inkuru yanyu, nyabuneka?

Both address one storyteller. The second version uses polite forms without changing who owns the story.
Can I keep the English word and say, “Please, mwampa inkuru yawe?”

It is understandable, but the forms mix two registers: mwampa is polite, while yawe is familiar. A consistent Kinyarwanda version is: Mwampa inkuru yanyu, nyabuneka? Here nyabuneka naturally replaces “please.”

messages.content: How does "umuhanda muto uri iburyo" change when I mean several roads?
Mu bwinshi uba: "Imihanda mito iri iburyo." The whole phrase changes together: "umuhanda" becomes "imihanda," "muto" becomes "mito," and "uri" becomes "iri."
Then give me a short direction saying: When you reach two small roads, take the one on the left.
Vuga uti: "Nugera ku mihanda ibiri mito, unyure mu muhanda w'ibumoso." "Imihanda ibiri mito" is plural. We return to singular "umuhanda" because the traveler chooses only one of the two roads.

messages.content: Ndashaka kubaza umuturanyi niba yateye ibigori mu murima wo hafi y'umugezi. Navuga nte?
Wamubaza uti: "Wateye ibigori mu murima wo hafi y'umugezi?" Iki kibazo gisobanutse kuko kivuga igihingwa n'umurima ushaka kumenya.
Yambwiye ko yateye ibishyimbo muri uwo murima, si ibigori. None nabaza nte igihe yabiteye?
Wabaza uti: "Wateye ryari ibishyimbo mu murima wo hafi y'umugezi?" Nongereye kuvuga ibishyimbo kuko ari byo yakosoye, kandi uwo murima ni wa wundi mwari muvuze.
Ntabwo yambwiye itariki. Ushobora kumbwira niba yarabiteye ku wa Mbere?
Oya, ibyo ntitwabimenya kuko atavuze itariki. Wamubaza uti: "Ese ibishyimbo wabiteye ku wa Mbere?" Icyo kibazo kirashaka amakuru; ntikivuga ko ku wa Mbere ari ukuri.

messages.content: How can I politely ask an employee at a public service desk to help me with a form?

You can say: "Mwiriwe. Mwamfasha kuzuza iyi fomu, mbese?" This is respectful and means, "Good afternoon. Could you help me fill out this form, please?" The greeting comes first, followed by the request and then mbese, which softens the request.
I was going to say, "Mwiriwe, can you help me kuzuza iyi form?" How can I avoid that code-switching without changing the meaning?

Say: "Mwiriwe. Mwamfasha kuzuza iyi fomu?" This keeps your meaning and avoids the English words. A slightly softer version is: "Mwiriwe. Mwamfasha kuzuza iyi fomu, mbese?" Here, iyi stays directly with fomu, and the request comes before mbese.

messages.content: Can you show me where nyinshi goes in two weather sentences, one about today and one about the rainy season?

Uyu munsi haguye imvura nyinshi. — A lot of rain fell today.
Mu gihe cy'imvura, hagwa imvura nyinshi. — A lot of rain falls during the rainy season.

Nyinshi follows the noun imvura in both sentences. The time phrase can move to the beginning, but imvura nyinshi stays together in that order.

messages.content: Mfite gahunda y'inama saa tatu. How do I ask one person, informally, where your office is?
Wamubaza uti: "Ibiro byawe biri he?" "Byawe" means "your," and "biri" agrees with "ibiro."
Ni ibiro by'umuyobozi, si ibyawe. Nshaka kubaza umukozi aho biri.
Noneho baza uti: "Ibiro by'umuyobozi biri he?" Nsubiyemo "ibiro" kuko ari iby'umuyobozi, atari iby'umukozi cyangwa ibyanjye.
Umukozi yavuze ko ibiro by'umuyobozi biri ku igorofa rya kabiri. Namubaza nte uko ngerayo mvuye ku muryango mukuru?
Mubaze uti: "Nagera nte ku biro by'umuyobozi mvuye ku muryango mukuru?" Ibi bikomeza kuvuga ibiro by'umuyobozi kandi ntibihimba inzira. Gahunda yawe y'inama iracyari saa tatu.

messages.content: Nandikira umuyobozi wanjye nti: "Madamu, ndashaka clarification ku kazi mwampaye." Nabivuga nte mu Kinyarwanda kiboneye kandi cyubashye?
Wavuga uti: "Madamu, mwansobanurira neza akazi mwampaye?" Ni uburyo bugufi kandi bwubashye bwo gusaba ibisobanuro, kandi busimbura ijambo clarification n'imvugo isanzwe y'Ikinyarwanda.
Nshaka no kumubaza niba agifite umwanya wo kubinsobanurira uyu munsi. Nabihuza nte?
Wandika uti: "Madamu, niba mugifite umwanya uyu munsi, mwansobanurira neza akazi mwampaye?" Mugifite na mwansobanurira byombi bihuye n'uburyo bwubashye wakoresheje ubwira umuyobozi wawe.

messages.content: What is the difference between “komeza” and “ongera” when giving a storyteller short directions?

Komeza means to continue the current action: Komeza kuvuga inkuru. — Continue telling the story.

Ongera tells someone to do something again: Ongera uvuge interuro ya nyuma. — Say the last sentence again.

So komeza moves the storytelling forward, while ongera repeats an earlier part.

messages.content: I want to practice asking for a birth certificate at the sector office. I say: "Ndashaka icyemezo ku murenge."
Say: "Ndashaka icyemezo cy'amavuko ku biro by'umurenge." "Cy'amavuko" identifies the document, while "ku biro by'umurenge" means at the sector office.
The clerk thinks I am asking for directions to the office, but I am already there. How do I correct that misunderstanding?
Vuga uti: "Oya, namaze kugera ku biro by'umurenge. Nshaka icyemezo cy'amavuko." This makes it clear that you have already arrived and are requesting the document.
Now the clerk asks where my old document is. It is inside my bag. Should I say "Iri ku gikapu cyanjye"?
Vuga uti: "Iri mu gikapu cyanjye." Use "mu" because the document is inside the bag; "ku gikapu" would place it on the bag.
Then I need to ask where to submit the old document, without assuming there is a particular desk or room. What should I say?
Baza uti: "Icyangombwa cya kera ngishyikirize he?" The word "he" asks where without assuming a desk or room, and "ngi-" refers back to "icyangombwa."

messages.content: Please make a natural Kinyarwanda sentence about directions using the exact words "ikarita yanjye" and explain why "ikarita wanjye" sounds unnatural.

"Narebye ikarita yanjye, mbona ko hoteli iri hafi ya sitasiyo." This means, "I looked at my map and saw that the hotel is near the station." Use yanjye with ikarita; wanjye does not agree with that noun. Exact required phrase: "ikarita yanjye".
Now make another sentence using the exact words "valisi yacu" and keep the same travel context.

"Tumaze kugera kuri sitasiyo, twafashe valisi yacu tujya kuri hoteli." This means, "After arriving at the station, we took our suitcase and went to the hotel." The possessive is yacu with valisi. Exact required phrase: "valisi yacu".

messages.content: At a shop, why can "Nashakaga iyi ihendutse" express a present choice? How is it different from "Ndashaka iyi ihendutse"?

Mu kiganiro n'umucuruzi, "Nashakaga iyi ihendutse" softens the present wish: "I would like the cheaper one." The context shows that the choice is current, not completed. "Ndashaka iyi ihendutse" is more direct: "I want the cheaper one." Contrast: "Nashakaga iyi ihendutse, niba bishoboka." versus "Ndashaka iyi ihendutse; ndayigura ubu." Here "iyi" refers to one item. For several items, the agreement changes: "Nashakaga izi zihendutse."

messages.content: Mu nteruro Yatetse isupu ye, who owns the soup and who cooked it?
Sinabimenya muri iyo nteruro yonyine. Yatetse does not name the cook, and ye can mean his or her. Ni nde watetse, kandi isupu ni iya nde?
Keza ni nyir'isupu, kandi Mutesi ni we wayitetse.
Noneho twavuga tuti: Mutesi yatetse isupu ya Keza. Mutesi is the cook, and ya Keza clearly shows that Keza owns the soup.

Nyuma agaruka mu rugo akaruhuka." Amina yatangiye saa kumi n'ebyiri n'igice za mu gitondo. Izina ry'uwo bagendanye ntirivugwa, bityo ntidushobora kurihimba. messages.content: Translate this as a formal community announcement: "We will meet at the village community hall tomorrow evening, but if it rains, we will move the dance rehearsal to Saturday."

"Ejo nimugoroba tuzahurira mu nzu mberabyombi y'umudugudu, ariko imvura nigwa, tuzasubika imyitozo yo kubyina tuyimurire ku wa Gatandatu." I used "imvura nigwa" for the natural condition "if it rains," and "tuyimurire" preserves the idea of moving the same rehearsal to another day.
Revise the plan as an informal message to one friend: "Actually, let's meet at the field tomorrow at 4:00 p.m. instead, and bring the two blue chairs again."

"Ahubwo, ejo tuzahurire ku kibuga saa kumi z'amanywa, kandi wongere uzane intebe ebyiri z'ubururu." The singular "wongere uzane" suits one friend and preserves "bring again." "Intebe ebyiri" keeps the exact number: two chairs.

messages.content: I want to ask a friend, "Did you cook the beans yesterday?" How do I say that informally?
Ask your friend: "Watetse ibishyimbo ejo?" Watetse addresses one person informally, and the sentence keeps the event in the past.
Now make it formal because I am asking a restaurant manager.
You can say: "Mumbabarire, mwatetse ibishyimbo ejo?" Mwatetse makes the address respectful while keeping the beans, the day, and the past meaning unchanged.
The manager replies, "Yes, I cooked them in the morning." How should the manager say that?
The manager can say: "Yego, nabitetse mu gitondo." The form bi in nabitetse refers to ibishyimbo.
Then I want to reply formally, "Thank you; they were delicious."
Say: "Murakoze, byari biryoshye." Byari agrees with ibishyimbo and shows that you are still talking about the beans.

Ryandikwa y'akazi, si ya akazi. Mu migemo, risomwa ya-ka-zi, ariko mu nyandiko apostrophe iguma hagati ya y na a; si akadomo. Inama ya Ange ni saa tatu. Afite na aritegura ni inshinga zivuga ibiri kuba ubu.

messages.content: How do I use cyiza in two farming contexts? I wrote Umurima ni cyiza and Igihingwa ni cyiza. Please explain the error.

Igihingwa ni cyiza is correct: it means The crop is good. With umurima, the descriptive form changes to match that noun: Umurima ni mwiza, meaning The field is good. So the contrast is:

Umurima ni mwiza.
Igihingwa ni cyiza.

The meaning good stays the same, but mwiza and cyiza agree with different nouns.

messages.content: Ku nshuti imwe nandika nti: "Ohereza ifoto." Nabivuga nte mu buryo bw'ubupfura ku muntu umwe? Nanone, ubwinshi bwa ifoto ni ubuhe, kandi Ohereza na Mwohereze bigabanywamo bite?

Mu buryo bw'ubupfura wavuga uti: "Mwohereze ifoto." Ubwinshi bwa ifoto ni amafoto. Mu nyandiko, amagambo agabanywamo atya: O-he-re-za na Mwo-he-re-ze. Guhindura Ohereza mo Mwohereze bihindura uwo ubwira, ariko ifoto ikomeza kuba imwe.
Niba nshaka amafoto menshi, mvuge nti: "Mwohereze amafoto"?
Yego, wavuga uti: "Mwohereze amafoto." Aha amafoto ni menshi, kandi interuro igabanywamo itya: Mwo-he-re-ze a-ma-fo-to. Imyandikire ya Mwohereze iguma ari ijambo rimwe.

messages.content: Write two natural Kinyarwanda sentences comparing housing alternatives. Sentence 1 must contain the exact word ihendutse. Sentence 2 must contain the exact word ahendutse. End each sentence with a full stop, then briefly explain the subject-marker agreement in English.

Iyi nzu ihendutse kurusha inzu iri hafi y'isoko.
Aya mazu ahendutse kurusha amazu ari ku muhanda munini.

The exact forms are ihendutse and ahendutse, and both sentences end with a period. The initial i in ihendutse agrees with singular inzu, while the initial a in ahendutse agrees with plural amazu.

messages.content: Interuro y'Icyongereza I am going home nayihindura nte mu Kinyarwanda? Ndashaka kugereranya uburyo bubiri.
Ibyo bishobora kuvugwa mu buryo butandukanye. Ese wamaze kuva aho wari uri, uri mu nzira ugana mu rugo, cyangwa uracyahari ariko uri hafi guhaguruka?

Ngiye gutaha ni yo ihuye neza n'ibyo wavuze, kuko ishimangira ko uri hafi guhaguruka. Ndataha na yo ishobora kuba itangazo ry'icyo ukora cyangwa ugiye gukora ubu, ariko ntigaragaza neza nk'iya mbere ko utaratangira urugendo.

messages.content: Read this short passage: Aline yasuye nyirasenge. Amaze kugera mu rugo, aramubwira ati: "Mwampa igikombe cy'amazi, ndabinginze?" What is Aline asking for, and what makes her request polite? Please contrast it with a direct request.

Aline is asking her aunt for a cup of water. "Mwampa igikombe cy'amazi, ndabinginze?" is polite because mwampa respectfully addresses her aunt and ndabinginze softens the request. Compare it with the direct command "Mpa igikombe cy'amazi." To one close friend, she could say "Wampa igikombe cy'amazi, ndakwinginze?" Here mw- changes to w- because the friend is addressed as one familiar person.

messages.content: How do I say "She did it after class" in Kinyarwanda?
What does "it" refer to, and does "after class" mean after the lesson ended or after she left the classroom? Without that context, Sinzi icyo yakoze only means "I do not know what she did."
It means that she returned a library book after the lesson ended.
You can say: Yasubije igitabo cyo mu isomero isomo rirangiye. Here, isomo rirangiye makes it clear that the lesson had ended.
Does that Kinyarwanda sentence say the exact time when she returned the book?
No. Interuro ivuga gusa ko yasubije igitabo isomo rirangiye; ntivuga isaha. An exact clock time would require more information.

1. Sinshobora kuvuga uwahawe akazi kuko nta makuru mashya mfite.
2. Raporo nshya ntigaragaza uwahawe akazi.

Nakoresheje neza "amakuru mashya" na "raporo nshya." "Mashya" ihuje na "amakuru," naho "nshya" ihuje na "raporo." Nta zina ryahimbwe.

messages.content: Mpa agace gato ko gusoma kerekeye kubungabunga ibidukikije. Gashyiremo igihe abaturage bazahurira, ariko ntikavuge uburyo bazagera aho bazatera ibiti.

Ku wa Gatandatu, abaturage bo mu Mudugudu wa Ubumwe bazatera ibiti ku nkombe z'umugezi. Bazahurira ku biro by'umudugudu saa mbili za mu gitondo, hanyuma bajye ku nkombe. Buri wese azazana icupa ry'amazi.

Mu gusoma, wibuke ko ijambo "saa" ryandikwa na a ebyiri.
Bazahura ryari, kandi bazagera ku nkombe bate?
Bazahura saa mbili za mu gitondo. Uburyo bazagera ku nkombe ntibuvugwa muri ako gace, bityo ntidushobora kumenya niba bazagenda n'amaguru cyangwa niba bazakoresha ubundi buryo.

messages.content: I need a message about tomorrow's conservation activity. Nanditse nti: "Ejo tuzaba..." ariko sinzi uko nkomeza.
What exactly will happen tomorrow, and who will receive the message: one friend or a community group? Ibyo bisobanuro birakenewe kugira ngo duhitamo amagambo n'urwego rw'ikinyabupfura bikwiye.
We will plant trees near the school. Mbwira inshuti imwe mu buryo busanzwe.
Wandika uti: "Ejo tuzatera ibiti hafi y'ishuri." "Tuzatera" expresses the future action directly, and the sentence is neutral and natural for a friend.
Now keep the same information, ariko nyandikira itsinda ry'abaturage mu buryo bwemewe.
Mu butumwa bwemewe, wavuga uti: "Tubamenyesheje ko ejo tuzatera ibiti hafi y'ishuri." "Tubamenyesheje" addresses the group respectfully, while "tuzatera" keeps the same future action.

messages.content: Nabwiye Keza ko ejo tuzahura saa tatu, hanyuma ndamwandikira nti: "Nzaguhamagara ageze ku biro." Nari nshatse kuvuga ko nzamuhamagara igihe jye nzaba ngeze ku biro. Nakosora nte?
Kosora uti: "Nzaguhamagara ngeze ku biro." Hindura "ageze" ibe "ngeze," kuko uwazaba ageze ku biro ari wowe uvuga. "Nzaguhamagara" yari isanzwe ikwiye kandi ikomeza kwerekeza kuri Keza.

messages.content: Give me a short Kinyarwanda passage about a visit to a public office, then correct my misunderstanding that the visitor traveled by bus and received a certificate at 9:00 a.m. Include a stated return time, but leave the means of transport unspecified. Please also point out one relevant vowel spelling.

Passage: Ku wa Gatatu, Keza yageze ku biro by'umurenge saa tatu za mu gitondo. Yari aje gufata icyemezo cy'amavuko. Umukozi yamusabye kugaruka saa munani.

Correction: Keza arrived at 9:00 a.m., but the passage does not say that she received the certificate then. She was asked to return at 2:00 p.m. It also does not state how she traveled, so we cannot say that she used a bus. In "saa", both letters a must be written.

messages.content: I am speaking to my friend Kamanzi. How can I replace the code-switching in "Hey Kamanzi, can you kureba igishushanyo cyanjye gishya?" with natural informal Kinyarwanda?

Say: "Kamanzi, wareba igishushanyo cyanjye gishya, ndakwinginze?" This is a natural request to one familiar person. "Gishya" agrees with the singular noun "igishushanyo," and the English words are unnecessary.
Now make the same request formal for a gallery director. Keep it as one new picture that belongs to me.

Say: "Muyobozi, mwareba igishushanyo cyanjye gishya, ndabinginze?" The respectful addressee changes "wareba" to "mwareba" and "ndakwinginze" to "ndabinginze." The phrase "igishushanyo cyanjye gishya" remains unchanged, so it still means one new picture belonging to you.

messages.content: Mu ishuri numvise ngo "umunyeshuri wiga buri munsi." What does that expression mean?

"Umunyeshuri wiga buri munsi" means "a student who studies every day." The part wiga buri munsi identifies the student by what the student does. Urugero: "Umwarimu ashima umunyeshuri wiga buri munsi."
How do I use the same pattern for plural students who ask questions?
Say: "abanyeshuri babaza ibibazo," meaning "students who ask questions." Compare umunyeshuri ubaza ibibazo with abanyeshuri babaza ibibazo. Urugero: "Umwarimu afasha abanyeshuri babaza ibibazo."

messages.content: Nagiye ku murenge gushaka icyemezo, ariko bambwiye ko dosiye yanjye ituzuye. Sinamenye icyo babuze.
Kubera ko utazi icyabuze, wabaza uti: "Ni iki kibura muri dosiye yanjye?" Dosiye yanjye igaragaza ko dosiye ari iyawe, ariko ntidushobora gukeka inyandiko ibura.
Bambwiye ko habuze kopi y'indangamuntu. Iyo ndangamuntu ni iya mama, kuko ari we dusabira icyemezo.
Noneho wavuga uti: "Muri dosiye yanjye haburamo kopi y'indangamuntu ya mama." Dosiye ni iyawe, ariko indangamuntu ni iya mama; izo nyirazo ntizivangwa.
Nshaka kubasubiza ko nzazana kopi yayo ejo. "Nzazana kopi yayo ejo" birumvikana?
Birumvikana, kuko yayo isubira ku ndangamuntu ya mama imaze kuvugwa. Ariko kugira ngo bititiranywa, wavuga neza uti: "Nzazana kopi y'indangamuntu ya mama ejo."

messages.content: Mu nteruro "Inzu nshya iri hafi y'iwacu," does iwacu mean "our neighborhood"? I may have misunderstood it.

Oya. Iwacu means "at our home" or "where we live," not specifically "our neighborhood." For "our neighborhood," you can say mu gace kacu: "Inzu nshya iri mu gace kacu." In hafi y'iwacu, write y'iwacu with an apostrophe because the following word, iwacu, begins with a vowel.

messages.content: Ndashaka kujya kuri gare, ariko sinshaka kunyura mu muhanda wa mukuru wanjye kuko urimo imodoka nyinshi. Nabivuga nte politely?

Wavuga uti: "Ndashaka kujya kuri gare, ariko nahisemo kutanyura mu muhanda mukuru w'iwacu kuko urimo imodoka nyinshi." In English: "I want to go to the station, but I chose not to take the main road near our home because it has heavy traffic." I changed "umuhanda wa mukuru wanjye," which means "my older sibling's road," to "umuhanda mukuru w'iwacu," the main road near our home.
Ni byo, nashakaga kuvuga the main road near our home. None se navuga nte ko nzanyura mu kayira kari inyuma y'inzu yacu?
Wavuga uti: "Nzanyura mu kayira kari inyuma y'inzu yacu." Here, "yacu" agrees with "inzu" and means "our." The sentence keeps your plan clear: you will use the path behind your home.
Niba mbisobanurira umushoferi mu kinyabupfura, nakoresha "iwacu" cyangwa "yacu" he?

Wavuga uti: "Mwambabarira, ntimunyure mu muhanda mukuru w'iwacu; munyure mu kayira kari inyuma y'inzu yacu." "Iwacu" follows the place phrase "umuhanda mukuru w'iwacu," while "yacu" directly shows that the house is ours. "Mwambabarira" makes the request respectful.

messages.content: Mu nteruro "Nagiye mu nama y'abakozi," how should I spell and read "y'abakozi"? Should it be "ya bakozi"?

The standard spelling is "y'abakozi": "Nagiye mu nama y'abakozi." The apostrophe shows that the final "a" of "ya" is omitted before "abakozi." For reading practice, you can divide the written form as "y'a-ba-ko-zi" and read it smoothly as one connected expression. The apostrophe is a spelling mark, not a separate sound.

messages.content: Nyabuneka, mwamfasha kumenya itandukaniro riri hagati ya "imbere ya" na "hafi ya" mu kubaza inzira?

"Imbere ya" yerekana ko ikintu kiri ahateganye n'uruhande rw'imbere rw'ikindi. "Hafi ya" yo ivuga ko ibintu bitegeranye, ariko ntivuge uruhande. Urugero: "Sitasiyo iri imbere ya banki" si kimwe na "Sitasiyo iri hafi ya banki." Mu nteruro isanzwe, banza icyo ushaka, ukurikizeho aho kiri: "Nyabuneka, mwanyereka sitasiyo iri hafi ya banki?"

messages.content: Ndashaka gusaba Aline kumfasha gusuzuma raporo ebyiri. Nabivuga nte mu kinyabupfura?
Wavuga uti: "Aline, wabona akanya ukamfasha gusuzuma raporo ebyiri?" Ibi birumvikana kandi ni uburyo bwubashye bwo gusaba ubufasha.
Mubyukuri ni raporo imwe gusa, iya mbere. Iya kabiri narayirangije. Nabikosora nte?
Vuga uti: "Aline, wabona akanya ukamfasha gusuzuma raporo ya mbere?" Dukuyemo raporo ebyiri kuko ubu ushaka ubufasha kuri raporo ya mbere gusa.
Nyuma nshaka kumubaza niba yayirebye. Interuro ngo "Aline, wayirebye?" irumvikana?
Irumvikana kuko raporo ya mbere yamaze kuvugwa, kandi -yi- iri muri wayirebye iyisimbura. Ariko mu kazi warushaho gusobanuka uti: "Aline, wabashije kureba raporo ya mbere?"

Practice them in short written chunks: za-we and wi-ge. In both words, w is written with the vowel that follows it. Then read the complete direction smoothly: Komeza wige kugira ngo ugere ku ntego zawe. Do not add an apostrophe to either zawe or wige.

messages.content: How do I say, "Could you please tell me which house is near the market?" in polite Kinyarwanda?

"Nyabuneka, mwambwira inzu iri hafi y'isoko iyo ari yo?"

"Mwambwira" makes the request respectful, while "iyo ari yo" preserves the meaning of "which one." A natural back-translation is: "Please, could you tell me which house is near the market?"

messages.content: Why does this sound unnatural: "Mfite gahunda gishya saa tatu"? I mean, "I have a new appointment at nine."
Say: "Mfite gahunda nshya saa tatu." The noun "gahunda" takes the agreeing adjective form "nshya," not "gishya." "Mfite" and "saa tatu" were already correct, so they stay unchanged.
What if I mean two new appointments at nine?
Say: "Mfite gahunda ebyiri nshya saa tatu." "Ebyiri" expresses two, and "nshya" still agrees with "gahunda."

messages.content: How can I casually tell a friend, "I'm resting at home because I'm tired"?
You can say: "Ndaruhuka mu rugo kuko naniwe." It is direct and natural with a friend; "mu rugo" means "at home."
How would I say the same thing more respectfully to an older colleague without changing the meaning?
Say: "Murakoze kumbaza. Ndaruhuka mu rugo kuko naniwe." The respectful tone comes from "Murakoze kumbaza," while the statement about you resting at home stays unchanged.
Could I code-switch and say, "Ndaruhuka kuri home kuko naniwe"?
It may be understood, but "kuri home" is avoidable and less natural here. Use the established Kinyarwanda location: "Ndaruhuka mu rugo kuko naniwe."

messages.content: Let's practice at a public library. I want to tell the librarian, "Ndashaka gukora borrow igitabo." How should I say it naturally?
Say: "Ndashaka gutira igitabo." This means, "I want to borrow a book." "Gutira" is the natural verb for borrowing. By contrast, "gufata igitabo" only means taking or picking up a book.
The librarian asks for my card. I answer, "Dore ikarita yanjye. I need iki gitabo uyu munsi." How can I avoid the English?
Say: "Dore ikarita yanjye. Nkeneye iki gitabo uyu munsi." This keeps your meaning: "Here is my card. I need this book today." "Nkeneye" naturally replaces "I need."

messages.content: Mu kazi, "ndakora" na "arakora" bitandukaniye he mu myandikire no mu gusoma?

Byombi byandikwa nk'ijambo rimwe. Kugira ngo ubisome buhoro: nda-ko-ra; a-ra-ko-ra. "Ndakora ku biro" bivuga ko ukora ari njye. "Arakora ku biro" bivuga ko ukora ari we. Mu nyandiko isanzwe, ntutandukanya ibice by'ayo magambo.
None se gereranya "turakora" na "barakora," kandi ukoreshe ijambo "abakozi."

Kugira ngo ubisome buhoro: tu-ra-ko-ra; ba-ra-ko-ra. "Turakora" ivuga njye n'abandi: "Turakora uyu munsi." "Barakora" ivuga abandi bantu: "Abakozi barakora uyu munsi." Mu nyandiko isanzwe, wandika "turakora" na "barakora" bifatanye.

messages.content: Nanditse nti: 'Ndi mu isoko uyu mugoroba,' nshaka kuvuga 'I am at the market this evening.' Kuki interuro yanjye yumvikana nk'idasanzwe?
Vuga uti: Ndi ku isoko uyu mugoroba. This means: I am at the market this evening. Ku isoko is the ordinary expression for being at the market; mu isoko emphasizes being inside the market.

messages.content: Why is "Abakinnyi mwiza baratsinze" incorrect? Please show me a contrast.

Use: Abakinnyi beza baratsinze. The form describing the players must match the plural noun abakinnyi. Compare: Umukinnyi mwiza yaratsinze. Abakinnyi beza baratsinze. The describing form changes from mwiza to beza, and the verb changes from yaratsinze to baratsinze.
Does the same kind of change happen with one bicycle and several bicycles?

Yes. Compare: Igare ryiza ririhuta. Amagare meza arihuta. With igare, the forms are ryiza and ririhuta. With the plural amagare, they become meza and arihuta, so both descriptions agree with the new noun.

messages.content: My friend texted, 'weather iri kuba cold.' Is that formal Kinyarwanda?

People may understand it in casual bilingual chat, but it mixes English with an English-shaped progressive construction. Natural Kinyarwanda is: Harakonje. A fuller neutral version is: Uyu munsi harakonje.
So when speaking politely to an older person, should I change it to 'Murakonje?'
No. Murakonje? asks the person or people whether they feel cold, so it changes the meaning. The weather statement stays Harakonje regardless of the addressee or level of politeness.

messages.content: What do "gishya" and "nshya" mean? I want to politely explain why I chose a book rather than a notebook.

Both mean "new," but they agree with different nouns: igitabo gishya and ikayi nshya. You can say: Nahisemo igitabo gishya aho guhitamo ikayi nshya, murakoze. For the nearby meaning "good," use igitabo cyiza and ikayi nziza.

messages.content: How do I say "appointment" in Kinyarwanda when describing an appointment with a tailor tomorrow morning? Please show the agreement forms too.

A natural expression is "gahunda yo kubonana," meaning an arranged appointment to meet someone. For example: "Gahunda yanjye yo kubonana n'umudozi izaba ejo saa tatu za mu gitondo." This means, "My appointment with the tailor will be tomorrow at 9:00 a.m." Here, "yanjye" and "izaba" agree with "gahunda." By contrast, "inama" usually means a meeting involving discussion: "Inama y'abaturage izaba ku wa Gatanu."

messages.content: Mwaramutse. How can I respectfully ask someone to help me practice talking about my morning routine?
Vuga uti: "Mwaramutse, mwamfasha kwitoza kuvuga ibyo nkora buri gitondo?" Mwamfasha means "could you help me" and is a concise, respectful request.
Mwamfasha kwitoza? Buri gitondo ndabyuka saa kumi n'ebyiri, hanyuma ngafata urugendo.
Ni byiza. Ku rugendo rwo kwishimisha, vuga uti: "Buri gitondo ndabyuka saa kumi n'ebyiri, hanyuma ngatembera." Gutembera means "to take a walk"; gufata urugendo usually suggests making a journey.

messages.content: In a morning-routine question, how do I pronounce and spell "n'iki" compared with "ni iki"? Please use both exact forms.

Write n'iki with an apostrophe when na comes before iki: "Wiyuhagira n'iki buri gitondo?" Here it means "With what do you bathe?" Write ni iki as two words: "Ni iki ukora buri gitondo?" Practice iki as i-ki; in n'iki, keep n' attached before i-ki, while ni iki keeps ni separate.
So in "Ni iki ukora buri gitondo?" I should not add an apostrophe, but in "Wiyuhagira n'iki buri gitondo?" I keep it?

Yego. "Ni iki ukora buri gitondo?" asks what you do. "Wiyuhagira n'iki buri gitondo?" asks what you use to bathe. The apostrophe belongs to n'iki in the second sentence; it is not a full stop or a quotation mark.

messages.content: Please translate this into English: "Inkuru y'inshuti yanjye yashimishije abana." What does the possessive expression show?
It means, "My friend's story delighted the children." In "y'inshuti yanjye," the first part links "inkuru" to its owner, while "yanjye" means "my" and describes "inshuti."
Noneho hindura interuro ivuge "My friend's stories delighted the children," but keep only one friend.

"Inkuru z'inshuti yanjye zashimishije abana." The natural English translation is, "My friend's stories delighted the children." Because "inkuru" now refers to multiple stories, the linking form changes from "y'inshuti" to "z'inshuti," and the verb changes from "yashimishije" to "zashimishije." "Inshuti yanjye" stays singular.

messages.content: Ese iyi nteruro irakwiye? "Nahisemo kujya ku kibuga n'amaguru aho kujyayo n'igare, kuko kugenda n'amaguru bimfasha kwitegura umukino." I want to explain my choice politely. Could I also replace nahisemo with natoranyije?

Ikosore gutya: "Nahisemo kujya ku kibuga n'amaguru aho kujyayo ku igare, kuko kugenda n'amaguru bimfasha kwitegura umukino." The only needed correction is n'igare to ku igare: n'amaguru means "on foot," while ku igare means "by bicycle." Nahisemo is natural here because you chose an action. Natoranyije more often means selecting a particular person or item from a group.

messages.content: Mu nkuru yo mu cyaro, nanditse "They gathered it." Translate that into Kinyarwanda and tell me whether they did it because it was ripe.

Ni iki bakusanyije, kandi bagikuye he? Without that information, I cannot choose confidently between "gukusanya," which focuses on bringing things together, and "gusarura," which refers to harvesting a crop. I also cannot say that ripeness caused the action because your sentence does not state a cause.
By "it" I mean ikawa. They removed the coffee crop from the plants, but the story does not say why.
Then use: "Basaruye ikawa." It means, "They harvested the coffee." "Gusarura" fits the stated farm action better than the broader "gukusanya." The reason for harvesting remains unknown.
Could I replace "gusarura" with "kweza" and write "Basaruye ikawa yeze" to prove that ripeness was the reason?

No. "Kweza" can describe producing or yielding a harvest, so it is not a direct replacement for the act of harvesting here. "Basaruye ikawa yeze" adds the fact that the coffee was ripe, but it still does not prove why they harvested it. Since the story gives neither fact, keep "Basaruye ikawa."

messages.content: How can I paraphrase "Mbyuka kare, maze nkajya ku kazi" without changing its basic meaning? Please show what happens to the verb forms.

You can say: "Nyuma yo kubyuka kare, njya ku kazi." Both versions mean that I wake up early and then go to work. After nyuma yo, kubyuka does not itself identify the person; njya shows that the understood person is "I." Contrast: "Nyuma yo kubyuka kare, ajya ku kazi" refers to he or she instead.
What if the subject is "we"? Does the agreement change in both versions?

Yes. Say: "Tubyuka kare, maze tukajya ku kazi." In the paraphrase, say: "Nyuma yo kubyuka kare, tujya ku kazi." The finite forms change from mbyuka and njya for "I" to tubyuka and tujya for "we"; kubyuka remains unchanged after nyuma yo.

messages.content: I am writing dialogue between a storyteller and another person at an arts event, but I do not know their relationship. Should the storyteller say "Wambwira icyo utekereza ku nkuru yanjye?" or "Mwambwira icyo mutekereza ku nkuru yanjye?" Can I add "please" at the end?

I cannot choose the register until the addressee is clearer. "Wambwira icyo utekereza ku nkuru yanjye?" addresses one person informally. "Mwambwira icyo mutekereza ku nkuru yanjye?" can address one person respectfully or several people. Adding "please" is usually unnecessary because "wambwira" or "mwambwira" already makes the request polite.
The storyteller is younger and is respectfully addressing one festival judge. The judge's reaction is unknown. Nakoresha iyi nteruro: "Mwambwira icyo mutekereza ku nkuru yanjye, please?"

A natural respectful line is: "Mwambwira icyo mutekereza ku nkuru yanjye?" Removing "please" gives the written dialogue a smoother Kinyarwanda rhythm without reducing politeness. The sentence asks for the judge's opinion but does not invent what that opinion is.

The action follows yahisemo, and the reason follows kuko. No tool is named, so adding one would go beyond the passage.

messages.content: How can I politely ask a driver to stop at the next stop, kandi interuro isanzwe nabwira incuti yaba iyihe?

Ku mushoferi wavuga uti: "Mwabasha guhagarara ku cyapa gikurikira?" This is a polite request. Ku ncuti imwe itwaye imodoka wavuga uti: "Wahagarara ku cyapa gikurikira?" "Mwa-" irubashye, naho "wa-" ihuje n'incuti imwe musanzwe muvugana.
Reka ngerageze: "Mwabasha guhagarara kuri next stop?" Ese byanditse neza nk'ikiganiro?

Birumvikana, ariko imvugo karemano ni: "Mwabasha guhagarara ku cyapa gikurikira?" "Ku cyapa gikurikira" replaces the avoidable English phrase "next stop." The short question also has a natural written rhythm.

messages.content: The referent is "ubutumwa." Which is correct for "I saw it": "Narayibonye" or "Narabubonye"? Please compare them with a telephone.

For "ubutumwa," say: "Narabubonye." The part "bu" points back to "ubutumwa." Contrast these examples:
"Nabonye ubutumwa. Narabubonye."
"Nabonye telefoni. Narayibonye."
The form changes because the object being replaced changes.
Now the objects are "amafoto" on that telephone. To say "I saw them," is "Narayabonye" correct?

Yes: "Amafoto ari kuri telefoni. Narayabonye." Here, "ya" points back to the plural noun "amafoto." It replaces the "bu" used for "ubutumwa," while the telephone remains the same one mentioned earlier.

messages.content: Buri gitondo mvuga nti: "Nkora prepare ikawa mbere yo gutangira akazi." Nabivuga nte mu Kinyarwanda gusa?
Vuga uti: "Buri gitondo ntegura ikawa mbere yo gutangira akazi." Ntegura replaces nkora prepare naturally and keeps the meaning "I prepare."
Noneho nshaka kongeraho nti: "Ndayinywa ku meza." Ese iyo nteruro irumvikana?
Yego, "Ndayinywa ku meza" irumvikana. Muri ndayinywa, -yi- isimbura ikawa yavuzwe mbere, bityo ntukeneye kongera kuyivuga.
Nyuma yaho mvuga nti: "Iyo ndayinyoye, I start akazi." Nakuramo English nte, kandi iyo ivuga iki hano?
Vuga uti: "Iyo maze kuyinywa, ntangira akazi." Kubera ko uvuga gahunda ya buri gitondo, iyo hano means "when" or "whenever." Ntirimo kuvuga isaha runaka.
Muri "Iyo maze kuyinywa," -yi- iracyasimbura ikawa, si igikombe, si byo? Sinigeze mvuga igikombe.
Ni byo. -yi- iracyasimbura ikawa, kuko ari yo yavuzwe. Nta gikombe cyigeze kivugwa, bityo ntidukwiye kugitekereza. Interuro yose ni: "Iyo maze kuyinywa, ntangira akazi."

messages.content: I want to summarize the community event. Nanditse nti: "Nyuma yi birori, twatashye." Ni gute nandika kandi ngasoma neza "y'ibirori"?

Andika uti: "Nyuma y'ibirori, twatashye." Mu nyandiko, "y'ibirori" ikoresha akabago kagufi hagati ya "y" na "ibirori," kandi nta mwanya ushyirwamo. Mu kuyisoma, kurikiza uko yanditse: "nyuma y'ibirori." Iri ni ihinduka ry'imyandikire; urukurikirane rw'amagambo rwo ruracyari "nyuma y'ibirori" mbere ya "twatashye."
Can I change the word order and write: "Twatashye nyuma y'ibirori"?

Yego. "Twatashye nyuma y'ibirori" ni interuro yuzuye kandi yanditse neza. Ibisobanuro by'ingenzi biracyari that we went home after the event; watangiye ku gikorwa "twatashye" aho gutangirira ku gihe "nyuma y'ibirori." Imyandikire ya "y'ibirori" ntiyahindutse.

messages.content: Yesterday I said, "Umukozi yafixingiye itara ryo ku muhanda." How can I say that without the English word?
Say: "Ejo, umukozi yasannye itara ryo ku muhanda." Gusana means "to repair," and yasannye means "repaired." It is more precise here than gukora, which can simply mean "to work" or "to make."
How would I say that two workers repaired the water pipe?
Say: "Ejo, abakozi babiri basannye umuyoboro w'amazi." Abakozi is plural, so the past-tense verb is basannye rather than yasannye.

messages.content: Bite, Eric? Umbwire igihe igitaramo cyo ku mudugudu gitangira.
Ibyo birakwiriye hagati y'inshuti. Ubajije umuyobozi mu buryo bwubashye wavuga uti: "Mwiriwe, mwambwira igihe igitaramo cyo ku mudugudu gitangira?"
None se navuga nti: "Bwana Muyobozi, uraza mu gitaramo?"
Mu mvugo yubashye, hindura "uraza" ube "muzaza": "Bwana Muyobozi, muzaza mu gitaramo?" Icyo ushaka kubaza ntigihindutse.
Nimubona umuyobozi, nzamubwira nti: "Urakoze kuduha amakuru."
Hano na ho koresha imvugo yubashye: "Nimubona umuyobozi, nzamubwira nti: 'Murakoze kuduha amakuru.'" "Murakoze" ni yo ihuje n'uburyo wamubajijemo.

messages.content: Write one formal Kinyarwanda sentence about restoring a wetland. Use first, then, and finally, but do not invent who will fund the work because I have not said.

Mbere na mbere, abaturage bazakuraho imyanda; hanyuma, bazatera ibyatsi byo muri ako gace; amaherezo, bazakurikirana uko igishanga gisubirana. English: First, residents will remove waste; then, they will plant grasses from that area; finally, they will monitor the wetland's recovery. The sequence uses Mbere na mbere, hanyuma, and amaherezo, and no funder is named.
Good. Now make it two sentences and add ariko to show that the planting date is still unknown.

Mbere na mbere, abaturage bazakuraho imyanda; hanyuma bazategura aho bazatera ibyatsi byo muri ako gace. Itariki yo gutera ibyatsi ntiramenyekana, ariko amaherezo bazakurikirana uko igishanga gisubirana. The two sentences use Mbere na mbere, hanyuma, ariko, and amaherezo, and they do not supply a planting date.

"Iyi gahunda yo guhura iracyakubereye? Niba itakubereye, bite se kuri iriya yo ku wa Gatanu?"

messages.content: I want to describe my routine. I wrote: "Buri gitondo njye mbyuka saa kumi n'ebyiri kandi nyuma njye ndakaraba kandi nyuma ndafata ifunguro rya mu gitondo." Why does it sound unnatural?

The repeated njye and kandi nyuma make the rhythm heavy. A smoother version is: "Buri gitondo mbyuka saa kumi n'ebyiri, ngakaraba, ngafata ifunguro rya mu gitondo." The linked verbs present the actions as a natural sequence.
Then I walk to work. Can you add that without making the sentence heavy again?
Yes: "Buri gitondo mbyuka saa kumi n'ebyiri, ngakaraba, ngafata ifunguro rya mu gitondo, hanyuma nkajya ku kazi n'amaguru." Hanyuma marks the final step clearly.
I actually mean Monday through Friday, not every morning. What should I change?
Replace buri gitondo with the exact range: "Kuva ku wa Mbere kugeza ku wa Gatanu, mbyuka saa kumi n'ebyiri, ngakaraba, ngafata ifunguro rya mu gitondo, hanyuma nkajya ku kazi n'amaguru."
Please give me the final version as a short dialogue answer to "What do you do in the morning?"

A: "Ukora iki mu gitondo?"
B: "Kuva ku wa Mbere kugeza ku wa Gatanu, mbyuka saa kumi n'ebyiri, ngakaraba, ngafata ifunguro rya mu gitondo, hanyuma nkajya ku kazi n'amaguru."

messages.content: Ndashaka kubwira inshuti nti: "Nakunze inkuru yawe. Wanyereka igitabo cyawe?" Nabivuga nte mu buryo bwiyubashye mbwira umwanditsi?
Wavuga uti: "Nakunze inkuru yanyu. Mwanyereka igitabo cyanyu?" Yanyu ijyana n'inkuru, naho cyanyu ikajyana n'igitabo.
Reka ngerageze: "Mwiriwe. Nakunze igitabo yanyu. Mwambwira uko mwatangiye kukandika?"
Kosora uti: "Mwiriwe. Nakunze igitabo cyanyu. Mwambwira uko mwatangiye kucyandika?" Hindura yanyu ibe cyanyu, kandi kukandika ibe kucyandika, kuko byombi byerekeza ku gitabo.
Mwiriwe. Nakunze igitabo cyanyu. Mwambwira uko mwatangiye kucyandika?
Ni byiza. Ubu interuro yawe iratunganye kandi irubashye. Umwanditsi ashobora gusubiza ati: "Murakoze kubaza. Nshobora kubabwira uko natangiye kucyandika."

messages.content: Please make one Kinyarwanda present-tense sentence using exactly "ibumoso" and "gare," and then give its English meaning.

"Uhindukira ibumoso ugeze kuri gare, hanyuma ugakomeza ugana ku isoko." It means: "You turn left when you reach the bus station, then continue toward the market." The sentence uses exactly "ibumoso" and "gare," and gives directions in the present tense.
Can you revise it so it also includes the exact word "ubu" and ends with a question mark?

"Ese ubu uhindukira ibumoso kuri gare, ugakomeza ugana ku isoko?" It means: "Do you now turn left at the bus station and continue toward the market?" It includes exactly "ubu," "ibumoso," and "gare," and ends with "?".

messages.content: Ndashaka kuvuga harvest mu Kinyarwanda. Nabivuga nte?
Harvest ishobora kuvuga igikorwa cyangwa ibyamaze kuboneka. Urashaka kuvuga igikorwa cyo gusarura, cyangwa umusaruro wabonetse? Tanga interuro kugira ngo mpitemo ijambo rikwiye.
Interuro ni iyi: We will harvest beans tomorrow. Ndashaka kuvuga igikorwa cyo gusarura.
Wavuga uti, Ejo tuzasarura ibishyimbo. Aha gusarura ni igikorwa, kandi tuzasarura yerekana ko ari twe tuzabikora ejo. Ntibikenewe kongeramo harvest.
None ndashaka kuvuga umusaruro wabonetse: The bean harvest was good.

Wavuga uti, Umusaruro w'ibishyimbo wari mwiza. Aha umusaruro ni ibishyimbo byabonetse nyuma yo gusarura, si igikorwa cyo gusarura. Bityo interuro ya mbere ikoresha gusarura, iya kabiri igakoresha umusaruro.

messages.content: When revising an appointment, what is the difference between guhindura gahunda and kwimura inama? Please contrast them in examples.

Guhindura gahunda means changing some part of a plan; kwimura inama specifically means moving a meeting to another time. Compare: "Twahinduye gahunda: tuzahurira ku biro aho guhurira kuri cafe." Here the place changes. "Twimuye inama yo ku wa Gatanu, tuyishyira ku wa Gatandatu." Here the meeting moves from Friday to Saturday.

messages.content: Ndashaka kuvuga ku giciro cy'ishati nti: "Iyi shati ni cheap."
Vuga uti: "Iyi shati irahendutse." Cheap usimbuze irahendutse; iyi na irahendutse byombi bihuje n'ishati.
Naho izi nkweto, navuga nti: "Izi nkweto irahendutse"?
Vuga uti: "Izi nkweto zirahendutse." Kubera ko wavuze izi nkweto, ukoresha zirahendutse, si irahendutse.
Nshaka kubibaza umucuruzi mu kinyabupfura. Nabivuga nte?
Uti: "Mwambwira niba izi nkweto zihendutse?" Izi nkweto na zihendutse biracyahuza, kandi mwambwira ituma ikibazo kiba icyiyubashye.

messages.content: Why do I say "Ukuguru kwanjye kurananiwe" but "Amaguru yanjye arananiwe" after a walk?

The related words change to match the noun. With singular "ukuguru," use "kwanjye" and "kurananiwe": "Ukuguru kwanjye kurananiwe nyuma yo kugenda." With plural "amaguru," use "yanjye" and "arananiwe": "Amaguru yanjye arananiwe nyuma yo kugenda." The meaning stays the same apart from one leg versus multiple legs.

Here maze means "then" or "after that" and connects the first action to the next one. The second action was watering the seeds: "Maze arazuhira." Hanyuma is a nearby sequencing word, and here it introduces the final action, returning home.

Soma iki gice: Keza yashakaga guhura na Samuel. Samuel yamuhaye amahitamo abiri: ku wa Kabiri saa tatu za mu gitondo cyangwa ku wa Gatatu saa cyenda z'amanywa. Keza yavuze ati: "Njye nzaza ku wa Gatatu saa cyenda z'amanywa, kuko ku wa Kabiri nzaba ndi ku kazi." Samuel aramusubiza ati: "Nanjye icyo gihe kirankwiriye."

Keza yahisemo ryari, kandi "nanjye" ivuga nde?
Keza yahisemo ku wa Gatatu saa cyenda z'amanywa. "Nanjye" ivuga Samuel, kuko ari we wasubizaga Keza. "Njye" yo ivuga Keza.
Bazahurira he? Ese ni ku kazi ka Keza?
Aho bazahurira ntihavugwa. Igice kivuga gusa igihe bahisemo; ntidushobora kwemeza ko bazahurira ku kazi ka Keza.

messages.content: How can I rewrite “Landlord ari gukora repair y'inzu muri neighborhood yacu” in natural Kinyarwanda, and where should the apostrophe go?

Say: “Nyir'inzu arimo gusana inzu yo mu gace dutuyemo.” Here, gusana means “to repair,” and agace dutuyemo means “the area where we live.” In standard spelling, Nyir'inzu has an apostrophe. Another natural example is: “Igisenge cy'inzu kirava.”

messages.content: Wanyigisha gukoresha “wowe” na “mwebwe” mu kiganiro kijyanye no kubungabunga ibidukikije?

Ku muntu umwe musanzwe mumenyeranye, wavuga uti: “Wowe urimo gutera igiti hafi y'umugezi.” Mu kubaha umuntu umwe, wavuga uti: “Mwebwe murimo gutera igiti hafi y'umugezi.” Igikorwa n'igiti ntibihinduka; “urimo” ihinduka “murimo” kugira ngo ihuze na “mwebwe.” Akenshi izo nsimburazina zikoreshwa iyo ushaka gushimangira uwo ubwira.
Mu nama yo kubungabunga ibidukikije, hari uvuga ati: “Mwebwe muri project lead.” Nakwirinda nte kuvanga indimi bitari ngombwa?

Wavuga uti: “Mwebwe muri umuyobozi w'igikorwa cyo kubungabunga ibidukikije.” Ibyo birumvikana neza mu Kinyarwanda. Ijambo ry'Icyongereza ryakoreshwa gusa niba ari izina ryihariye itsinda ryemeranyijeho; bitabaye ibyo, “umuyobozi w'igikorwa” rirahagije.

messages.content: Nashakaga gusaba inshuti yanjye ko ingeza kwa mama. Nanditse nti: “Nyabuneka, mpa imodoka yawe ingeze kwa mama.” Iyi nteruro irakwiye?

Wavuga uti: “Nyabuneka, wamfasha ukangeza kwa mama mu modoka yawe?” Imvugo “mpa imodoka yawe” yumvikanisha ko ushaka ko aguha cyangwa akagutiza imodoka. “Ukangeza” yo igaragaza neza ko ushaka ko akujyana, kandi “mu modoka yawe” igaragaza uburyo muzagenda.
Ndabyumvise. None se niba nshaka ko atwara njye na mushiki wanjye, nabivuga nte ntahinduye icyo nshaka kumubwira?
Wavuga uti: “Nyabuneka, wadufasha ukatugeza kwa mama mu modoka yawe?” “Du” na “tu” byerekeza kuri wowe na mushiki wawe. Interuro iracyamusaba kubatwara; ntimusaba kubatiza imodoka.

messages.content: Soma uyu mwandiko: "Abaturage bateganya umunsi wo gusukura aho batuye. Bashoboraga guhura ku wa Gatandatu saa tatu za mu gitondo cyangwa ku Cyumweru saa munani. Bahisemo ku wa Gatandatu saa tatu za mu gitondo kuko benshi ari bwo baboneka. Aho bazahurira ntiharamenyekana." Answer in English: Which option did they choose, why did they choose it, and where will they meet? Does "bahisemo" mean "they chose" or "they visited"?

They chose Saturday at saa tatu za mu gitondo, or 9:00 a.m., because most people are available then. The meeting place is not given; the passage says it is not yet known. "Bahisemo" means "they chose," which fits the comparison between the two options.

messages.content: What is the difference between "Abaturage batera ibiti buri mwaka" and "Abaturage barimo gutera ibiti ubu"? Also, what changes if I replace "abaturage" with "umuturage"?

"Abaturage batera ibiti buri mwaka" describes a repeated present habit: "Residents plant trees every year." "Abaturage barimo gutera ibiti ubu" presents the action as underway now: "Residents are planting trees now."

With one resident, the agreement changes: "Umuturage atera ibiti buri mwaka" and "Umuturage arimo gutera ibiti ubu." Thus, "batera/barimo" matches plural "abaturage," while "atera/arimo" matches singular "umuturage."

messages.content: I am practicing questions about a story. We know that Aline finished a mural on Friday, but the story does not say where. How do I ask when and where she finished it?

You can ask: “Aline yarangije igishushanyo cyo ku rukuta ryari?” for “When did Aline finish the mural?” For the location, ask: “Aline yakirangije he?” The marker “ki” in yakirangije refers to igishushanyo.
What answers can I give to those two questions from the information we have?
For the first question: “Yakirangije ku wa Gatanu.” For the second, we cannot give a location because none was provided. You can say: “Aho yakirangirije ntihavuzwe.”
Is “Aline yakirangije he ku wa Gatanu?” a correct question? Could I answer “Mu nzu ye”?
Yes, “Aline yakirangije he ku wa Gatanu?” is correct; it asks for the unknown location while retaining Friday. You cannot answer “Mu nzu ye,” because neither a house nor its ownership was mentioned.

messages.content: My draft is "Ejo I have a meeting na Aline saa munani." How do I naturally say, "I will meet Aline again tomorrow at exactly 2:00 p.m."?
Say: "Nzongera guhura na Aline ejo saa munani zuzuye z'amanywa." Here, "nzongera guhura" preserves "will meet again," while "saa munani zuzuye z'amanywa" gives the exact time, 2:00 p.m.
The time changed. How do I say, "We moved that appointment to exactly 3:00 p.m., but I will still meet Aline again tomorrow"?
Say: "Twimuye iyo gahunda tuyishyira ejo saa cyenda zuzuye z'amanywa, ariko ejo nzongera guhura na Aline." This keeps the revised time, 3:00 p.m., and "nzongera" still carries the meaning of "again."

messages.content: Ejo nagiye gutembera kuva kuri hoteli kugeza ku isoko.
Mu buryo busanzwe wavuga uti: "Ejo navuye kuri hoteli njya ku isoko n'amaguru." Ibi byerekana neza aho watangiriye n'aho wari ugiye.
Ngeze ku isoko, nabajije umugore aho isomero iri.
Ni byiza. Kosora gusa uti: "Ngeze ku isoko, nabajije umugore aho isomero riri." Ijambo "riri" rihura na "isomero."
Yambwiye ko isomero riri hagati ya banki na pariki. Nanyuze hafi ya pariki.
Ibyo birumvikana neza. "Hagati ya banki na pariki" herekana aho isomero riri, naho "hafi ya pariki" herekana aho wanyuze. Wahageze ryari?
Nahageze saa kumi, ariko isomero ryari rifunze, nuko nsubira kuri hoteli.
Birumvikana. "Nahageze" irasubira ku isomero mwari mumaze kuvuga, kandi "nsubira kuri hoteli" igaragaza neza aho wasubiye.

Soma iki gice: "Mu isomero ry'ishuri harimo ibitabo bitatu bishya n'ikaye imwe nshya. Sara ahitamo ibitabo bibiri bishya byo gusoma nimugoroba."

What does Sara choose, and what color are the items she chooses?

messages.content: Give me a short Kinyarwanda passage about a relaxing walk. Include the exact time and number of trees, but do not say who accompanied the person. Then ask me three comprehension questions in English.

“Ku wa Gatandatu saa moya za mu gitondo, Keza yagiye gutembera mu busitani. Yabonye ibiti bitatu n'indabo nyinshi. Nyuma y'iminota makumyabiri, yasubiye mu rugo aruhutse.”

Questions: What time did Keza go for the walk? How many trees did she see? Who went with her?
Keza yagiye saa moya za mu gitondo kandi yabonye ibiti bitatu. I think she went with her sister.

Your first two answers are supported: “Yagiye saa moya za mu gitondo” and “Yabonye ibiti bitatu.” The passage does not mention a sister or any companion, so we cannot say who went with Keza. Notice the plural pair: igiti becomes ibiti, and “three trees” is ibiti bitatu.

messages.content: I tried to say, “She told me that I am well today”: “Yambwiye ko umeze neza uyu munsi.” Is that correct?
The corrected sentence is: “Yambwiye ko meze neza uyu munsi.” Keep yambwiye because it correctly means “she told me.” Change umeze to meze because the person who is well is “I,” not “you.”
If I mean, “She told you that she is well today,” can I say: “Yambwiye ko ameze neza uyu munsi”?
Say: “Yakubwiye ko ameze neza uyu munsi.” Change yambwiye to yakubwiye because the person being told is now “you.” “Ameze” is already correct because it refers to “she.”

messages.content: Ejo nasuye inshuti yanjye mu mudugudu mushya.

Nabonye amazu meza, ariko sinzi igihe yubatswe. Navuga ko yubatswe umwaka ushize?
Oya, ntuvuge umwaka ushize kuko utabizi. Vuga uti: "Nabonye amazu meza, ariko sinzi igihe ayo mazu yubatswe."
None navuga nti: "Ejo nasuye inshuti yanjye, nabonye amazu meza, ariko sinamenye igihe ayo mazu yubatswe."
Yego, iyo nteruro irumvikana neza. "Nasuye," "nabonye," na "sinamenye" byose bivuga ibyabaye mu gihe cyashize, kandi ntiwongeyemo igihe utazi.

messages.content: Mu gutegura gahunda y'umunsi, "kubanza" na "hanyuma" bitandukaniye he, kandi mbishyira he mu nteruro?

"Kubanza" yerekana igikorwa ukora mbere y'ikindi, kandi ikurikirwa n'igikorwa: "Nzabanza gukora isuku, hanyuma njye ku isoko." "Hanyuma" itangiza igikorwa gikurikiraho. Uhinduye gahunda wavuga uti: "Nzabanza kujya ku isoko, hanyuma ngaruke nkore isuku." Naho "mbere yo" igereranya ibihe: "Mbere yo kujya ku isoko, nzakora isuku."

messages.content: Ejo nagiye kuri gare gufata bisi ijya i Musanze.
Ni interuro nziza. Wategereje bisi he?
Nategereje mu cyapa hafi ya gare.
Vuga uti: "Nategereje ku cyapa hafi ya gare." Dukoresha "ku cyapa" aho gukoresha "mu cyapa." Bisi igeze, wicaye he?
Bisi igeze, nicaye ku ntebe iri imbere.
Birumvikana. Uburyo busanzwe kurushaho ni: "Bisi imaze kugera, nicaye ku ntebe y'imbere." Wayivuyemo ugeze he?
Navuyemo ku isoko, hanyuma njya mu iduka.
Wavuga neza uti: "Navuyemo ngeze ku isoko, hanyuma njya mu iduka." "Ku isoko" ni ho waviriye muri bisi, naho "mu iduka" ni ho wahise ujya.

messages.content: Mu gikorwa cy'abaturage, nabwira umuturanyi nti: 'Wamfasha kuri iyi event?' Ndashaka kubivuga mu Kinyarwanda kandi mu buryo bwiyubashye.

Wavuga uti: 'Wamfasha muri iki gikorwa?' Ijambo 'event' risimburwa na 'igikorwa,' kandi 'iki' kijyana na 'igikorwa.' Niba ubwira umuntu ushaka guha icyubahiro, wavuga uti: 'Mwamfasha muri iki gikorwa?'
Niba icyo gikorwa twaramaze kukivugaho, nakoresha 'icyo'? Kandi noneho ndabwira abantu babiri.
Yego. Vuga uti: 'Mwamfasha muri icyo gikorwa?' 'Mwa-' ibwira abantu babiri, naho 'icyo' kigaruka ku gikorwa mwamaze kuvugaho. Igikorwa kiracyari kimwe.

messages.content: How do I ask whether someone cooked beans, as opposed to asking what they cooked?

To ask for a yes-or-no answer, say: "Ese watetse ibishyimbo?" This means "Did you cook beans?" To ask which food the person cooked, say: "Watetse iki?" This means "What did you cook?" In the second question, "iki" replaces the food that is not yet known.

messages.content: Mfite intego yo kunoza Igifaransa. Ndagereranya kwiga iminota mirongo itatu buri mugoroba no kwiga amasaha atatu ku wa Gatandatu. Aha nakoresha "intego," "umugambi" cyangwa "gahunda"?

Kunoza Igifaransa ni intego, kuko ari icyo ushaka kugeraho. Kwiga buri mugoroba cyangwa ku wa Gatandatu ni gahunda, kuko bigena uko n'igihe uziga. Umugambi ni icyo wiyemeje gushyira mu bikorwa, ariko "gahunda" ni ryo jambo risobanutse kurushaho hano.
Nahisemo uburyo bwa mbere kuko nshaka gukomeza kwiga buri munsi. Ese "gukomeza" no "guhoraho" bisobanura kimwe?

Si kimwe neza. "Gukomeza kwiga" ni kutareka kwiga; "guhoraho" ni ukumara igihe kirekire cyangwa kutarangira. Ku cyemezo cyawe, birasanzwe kuvuga uti: "Nziga iminota mirongo itatu buri mugoroba kugira ngo nkomeze kwiga buri munsi."
None nandike nti: "Nahisemo uburyo bwa mbere kuko buroroshye gukurikiza kurusha ubwa kabiri"?

Igitekerezo cyawe kirumvikana. Interuro isobanutse kurushaho ni iyi: "Nahisemo uburyo bwa mbere kuko ari bwo bworoshye gukurikiza buri munsi kurusha uburyo bwa kabiri." Gusubiramo "uburyo bwa kabiri" bituma ikigereranywa kititiranywa n'ikindi kintu.

messages.content: Interuro yanjye ni iyi: "Mbanza kuruhuka, hanyuma mbere nkanywa amazi." Kuki yumvikana nabi?
Wayikosora uti: "Mbanza kuruhuka, hanyuma nkanywa amazi." "Mbanza" yamaze kwerekana igikorwa cya mbere, naho "hanyuma" ikerekana igikurikiraho. Ni yo mpamvu "mbere" idakenewe nyuma ya "hanyuma."
Nyuma yabyo nshaka kuvuga nti: "Nyuma y'ibyo, nuko njya gutembera." Ibyo byo birakwiye?
Vuga uti: "Nyuma y'ibyo, njya gutembera." Ushobora no kuvuga uti: "Hanyuma njya gutembera." "Nuko" ntikenewe hano, kuko "nyuma y'ibyo" yamaze kwerekana ikurikirana ry'ibikorwa.

messages.content: In the sentence "Abahinzi bazasarura ibigori mu kwezi gutaha," what does "bazasarura" mean, and on what exact date will they harvest?

"Bazasarura" means "they will harvest." The sentence places the harvest in the future: "Abahinzi bazasarura ibigori mu kwezi gutaha." It contrasts with "bazatera ibigori," meaning "they will plant maize." The exact harvest date is not given; the sentence says only "next month."

messages.content: Buri gitondo ntegereza bisi aho zihagarara. Iyo ije, ndayinjiramo. Ese "-yi-" muri "ndayinjiramo" isimbura iki?
"-yi-" isimbura "bisi": winjira muri bisi. Interuro yawe irumvikana neza kandi ikomeza kuvuga urugendo rwa buri gitondo.
Nyuma mbona intebe irimo ubusa, ndayicaraho kugeza bisi igeze aho nkorera. Aha "-yi-" iracyasimbura bisi?
Oya. Muri "ndayicaraho," "-yi-" isimbura "intebe," si "bisi," kuko ari intebe wicaraho. Muri "bisi igeze aho nkorera," wongeye kuvuga izina "bisi" ku buryo icyo ushaka kuvuga gisobanutse.

messages.content: Translate this into natural English: 'Mbabarira, mwambwira niba iyi bisi ijya i Huye, kandi niba ihaguruka mbere ya saa yine za mu gitondo?' Also, what makes the request polite?

Excuse me, could you tell me whether this bus goes to Huye and whether it leaves before 10:00 a.m.?

'Mbabarira' politely gets the listener's attention, while 'mwambwira' is naturally rendered as 'could you tell me' rather than the more direct 'tell me.' The translation preserves both questions: the destination and the departure time.

messages.content: Soma aka gace: "Ku wa Gatandatu saa kumi z'umugoroba, Aline yari ananiwe nyuma yo kwiga. Yafashe akaruhuko, anywa amazi, maze mushiki we amuzanira igitabo. Aline aramubwira ati: 'Ndakigusubiza ejo.'" At what time was Aline tired, and what did her sister bring her?
Aline yari ananiwe saa kumi z'umugoroba, ni ukuvuga 4:00 p.m. Mushiki we yamuzaniye igitabo. Those are the only requested details stated in the passage.
Why does "Mushiki we amuzanira Aline igitabo" sound unnatural when I retell the passage?

Mu- in amuzanira already represents Aline, so repeating Aline is unnecessary in a neutral sentence. Say either "Mushiki we amuzanira igitabo" or, with the name stated, "Mushiki we azanira Aline igitabo."

messages.content: Mu kuvuga imirimo yo mu murima, "hanyuma" risobanura iki? Ritandukaniye he na "nyuma yo"?

"Hanyuma" means "then" or "after that" and links two actions: "Twabanje guhinga, hanyuma dutera imbuto." "Nyuma yo" means "after" and is followed by an action or event: "Nyuma yo gutera imbuto, twavomerera umurima." So, use "hanyuma" to continue a sequence and "nyuma yo" to introduce what happened before the next action.

messages.content: How do I say, "I do not draw; I tell stories"?

I want to answer, "I don't tell long stories; I tell short stories."
You can answer: "Simbara inkuru ndende; mbara inkuru ngufi." This keeps the same contrast: you negate long stories, then state that you tell short ones.

None se navuga nti: "Nta birungo nashyizemo"?

Sinzi niba narashyizemo umunyu, ariko natetse ibishyimbo.

messages.content: Read this passage: “Ku wa Kane, Keza yagombaga kuganira n'umwarimu we. Umwarimu yamuhaye amahitamo abiri: saa tatu za mu gitondo cyangwa saa munani z'amanywa. Keza yahisemo saa munani kuko saa tatu yari kuba ari mu isomo. Bemeranyije guhurira ku ishuri, ariko ntibavuze icyumba.” Which time did Keza choose, and why?
Keza yahisemo saa munani z'amanywa, or 2:00 p.m. She rejected saa tatu za mu gitondo because she would be in class at that time.
What room number did they choose? Also, what does “yari kuba ari mu isomo” mean in this context?
Nta nimero y'icyumba ivugwa muri uwo mwandiko. In context, “yari kuba ari mu isomo” means “she would be in class”; it explains why the morning option did not suit her.

messages.content: Mu mupira w'amaguru, amagambo "gutsinda" no "kunyagira" atandukaniye he? Mpa ingero zoroshye.

"Gutsinda" ni ukubona amanota cyangwa ibitego byinshi kurusha uwo mukina. "Kunyagira" ni gutsinda ku buryo burushijeho kugaragara, akenshi harimo ikinyuranyo kinini cy'ibitego. Urugero: "Ikipe yacu yatsinze indi ibitego bibiri kuri kimwe." Ariko wavuga uti: "Ikipe yacu yanyagiye indi ibitego bitanu ku busa." Buri kunyagira ni ugutsinda, ariko gutsinda kose si ukunyagira.

messages.content: Ku wa Gatandatu, Keza yasuye mukuru we Amina. Eric yashatse kubasanga, ariko ntiyaje kuko yari ku kazi. Mfasha gukora incamake irimo impakanyi.
Ushobora kuvuga uti: "Keza yasuye Amina, ariko Eric ntiyaje." In English: "Keza visited Amina, but Eric did not come." Impakanyi "ntiyaje" yerekeza kuri Eric.
Nagerageje kuvuga nti: "Keza ntiyasuye Amina, kandi Eric yaraje." Ese birahuye n'inkuru?
Oya. Iyo nteruro ihindura amakuru yombi. Incamake ihuye n'inkuru ni: "Keza yasuye Amina, ariko Eric ntiyaje." Keza yarasuye Amina; Eric ni we utaraje.
Muri "mukuru we Amina," ijambo "we" ryerekeza kuri nde? Hanyuma umpe incamake ya nyuma mu Cyongereza.
Muri iyo nteruro, "we" ryerekeza kuri Keza: Amina ni mukuru wa Keza. Final summary: "On Saturday, Keza visited her older sister Amina, but Eric did not come because he was at work."

messages.content: Kuki tuvuga ngo “Umutsima urashyushye,” ariko tukavuga ngo “Ibirayi birashyushye”?

Ijambo rivuga uko ibiryo bimeze rihinduka rigahuza n'izina. Tuvuga ngo “Umutsima urashyushye,” ariko tukavuga ngo “Ibirayi birashyushye.” Bityo, “ura-” ikoreshwa hamwe n'umutsima, naho “bira-” igakoreshwa hamwe n'ibirayi.
None se navuga nte ku isupu imwe no ku masupu menshi?
Wavuga uti: “Isupu imwe irashyushye,” naho ku bwinshi uti: “Amasupu menshi arashyushye.” Iyo “isupu” ihindutse “amasupu,” “irashyushye” na yo ihinduka “arashyushye.”

messages.content: Why do people say "Bisi irahaguruka kare" but "Bisi zirahaguruka kare"?

The first sentence means one bus leaves early: "Bisi irahaguruka kare." The subject marker is "i-." The second means multiple buses leave early: "Bisi zirahaguruka kare." For plural buses, the marker changes to "zi-." Mu nteruro zombi, bisi ni zo zihaguruka.
How would I politely say, "I chose the buses because they leave early"?
Wavuga uti: "Nahisemo bisi kuko zihaguruka kare." Here you mean multiple buses, so "zi-" in "zihaguruka" refers back to them. If you meant one bus, you would say: "Nahisemo bisi kuko ihaguruka kare."

Soma iki gika, hanyuma usubize ibibazo.

Ku wa Gatandatu, Keza yavuye mu rugo saa mbili za mu gitondo. Yabanje kunyura imbere y'iposita, maze akomeza kugenda kugera ku isomero. Hanyuma yafashe bisi igana ku isoko. Ageze ku isoko, yaguze imbuto, nyuma abaza umucuruzi inzira igana kuri gare.

Keza yavuye mu rugo saa ngahe? Ni ibihe bikorwa bibiri yakoze mbere yo kubaza inzira? Ibara rya bisi ryari irihe? Ijambo "igana" risobanura iki aho ryakoreshejwe kuri bisi no ku nzira?

Keza yavuye mu rugo saa mbili za mu gitondo. Mbere yo kubaza inzira, yafashe bisi, hanyuma agura imbuto. Ibara rya bisi ntirivugwa muri iki gika. "Igana" yerekana aho ikintu kerekeza: bisi yerekezaga ku isoko, naho inzira yerekezaga kuri gare.

messages.content: Buri gitondo ndabyuka saa kumi n'ebyiri, hanyuma ngakora shower. Nabivuga nte mu Kinyarwanda gusa?

Vuga uti: "Buri gitondo ndabyuka saa kumi n'ebyiri, hanyuma nkiyuhagira." "Kwiyuhagira" ni ko kuvuga icyo washakaga kuvuga. "Kubyuka" ni kuva mu bitotsi, naho "guhaguruka" akenshi ni kuva aho wari wicaye cyangwa uryamye.
None se nshobora kuvuga nti: "Ndabyuka, ariko nkomeza kuryama; nyuma ndahaguruka"?
Yego, birumvikana neza. "Ndabyuka" bivuga ko ibitotsi bishize, naho "ndahaguruka" bivuga ko uva mu buriri. Urugero: "Mbyuka saa kumi n'ebyiri, ariko mpaguruka saa moya."

messages.content: Nateye igiti kimwe ku ishuri. Navuga nte ko icyo giti ari icyanjye?
Uvuga uti: “Iki ni igiti cyanjye.” Iyo ari byinshi, uvuga uti: “Ibi ni ibiti byanjye.” Cy- ikoreshwa kuri igiti, naho by- igakoreshwa kuri ibiti.
Amababi wacyo aracyari mato. Ni byo?
Hindura wacyo ube yacyo: “Amababi yacyo aracyari mato.” Amababi ni yo agena y-, kandi yacyo yerekana ko ayo mababi ari ay'igiti wavuze.
Noneho navuga nti: “Amababi yacyo aracyari mato, ariko igiti cyanjye kirakura.”
Ni byo. “Yacyo” iracyerekeza kuri cya giti kimwe wateye, naho “cyanjye” ikerekana ko igiti ari icyawe.

messages.content: Mu nteruro "Twubatse ikigega cy'amazi," why do we write "cy'amazi" instead of "cya amazi"? Mpa n'izindi ngero zijyanye no kubungabunga ibidukikije.

Iyo "cya" cyangwa "ya" ikurikiwe n'ijambo ritangirwa n'inyajwi, inyajwi ya nyuma irakurwaho: "Twubatse ikigega cy'amazi." Ariko iguma imbere y'ingombajwi: "Twubatse ikigega cya peteroli." Dore irindi tandukaniro: "Twakusanyije imyanda y'amababi," ariko "Twakusanyije imyanda ya pulasitiki." The agreement also changes with the noun: "ikigega" takes "cya," while "imyanda" takes "ya."

messages.content: Please translate: "The new employees attend two meetings every Monday." I tried: "Abakozi nshya bitabira inama bibiri buri wa Mbere." Why does it sound unnatural?

A natural translation is: "Abakozi bashya bitabira inama ebyiri buri wa Mbere." The plural noun "abakozi" requires "bashya," and plural "inama" takes "ebyiri." That is why "nshya" and "bibiri" do not agree correctly here.

"Imipira ibiri mishya ni mito." Imipira is plural, so "new" becomes mishya and "small" becomes mito. These forms agree with imipira, while ibiri preserves the exact number, two.

messages.content: Nanditse nti: "Mu rainy season, imvura igwa in Kigali." Nabikosora nte mu Kinyarwanda?
Wavuga uti: "Mu gihe cy'imvura, imvura igwa i Kigali." Rainy season yasimbujwe igihe cy'imvura, naho in Kigali ihinduka i Kigali. Ibindi wari wanditse ni byo.

Ikosorwa ni: "Mu mpeshyi tujya ku musozi kubera ko haba hashyushye." Summer yasimbujwe impeshyi. Ku musozi na kubera ko haba hashyushye byari bisanzwe ari byo, bityo ntibihinduka.

messages.content:
Soma iki gika:

Ku wa Kabiri saa tatu za mu gitondo, abaturage bo mu Mudugudu wa Kabeza bagiye ku biro by'umurenge gusaba serivisi y'amazi. Umukozi yarababwiye ati: "Izi documents muzizane ejo, kandi iyi form muyuzuze neza."

At what time did the residents go? Repair the unnecessary English words while keeping noun agreement correct. How much did the service cost?

They went at saa tatu za mu gitondo, or 9:00 a.m. The repaired instruction is: “Muzane izi nyandiko ejo, kandi mwuzuze neza iyi fishi.” “Izi” agrees with plural “nyandiko,” while “iyi” agrees with singular “fishi.” Nta giciro cya serivisi cyavuzwe muri iki gika, so its cost cannot be determined.

messages.content: Ndimo kwandika inkuru. Imvugo "nyuma yo" nayikoresha nte mvuga ko nabanje kumva inkuru, hanyuma nkayishushanya?

Vuga uti: "Nyuma yo kumva inkuru, narayishushanyije." Ushobora no kuvuga uti: "Nashushanyije inkuru nyuma yo kuyumva." Mu ya mbere, icyo wabanje gukora kiza mbere; mu ya kabiri, icyo wakoze nyuma ni cyo kibanza kuvugwa.
Nagerageje nti: "Nyuma yo inkuru kumva, narayishushanyije." Iryo tondeka rirakwiye?
Oya. Vuga uti: "Nyuma yo kumva inkuru, narayishushanyije." Nyuma ya "nyuma yo," ubanza igikorwa "kumva," ugakurizaho icyo wumvise, ari cyo "inkuru."

messages.content: I rent one house near the market. Nshaka kuvuga “my house” mu Kinyarwanda.
Say “inzu yanjye.” A full sentence is: “Inzu yanjye iri hafi y'isoko.” Yanjye shows that the house is yours.
Inzu yanjye iri hafi y'isoko. My neighbor has a garden. Nabivuga nte?
Vuga uti: “Umuturanyi wanjye afite ubusitani.” Here, wanjye means “my” because it describes umuturanyi.
Ubusitani bwe buri inyuma y'inzu. I mean that the garden belongs to my neighbor, but is the house clear?
Ubusitani bwe burumvikana, ariko inzu ntiramenyekana neza. Ese ushaka kuvuga inyuma y'inzu ye, their house, cyangwa inyuma y'inzu yawe, your house?
I mean their house: inyuma y'inzu ye.
Noneho interuro yuzuye ni: “Ubusitani bwe buri inyuma y'inzu ye.” Bwe yerekeza ku busitani bw'umuturanyi, kandi ye ikerekana ko inzu na yo ari iy'uwo muturanyi.

messages.content: Why does "Nteka ibiryo iryoshye" sound unnatural if I mean "I cook tasty food"?

Say: "Nteka ibiryo biryoshye." Both iryoshye and biryoshye mean "tasty," but the form must match the noun. Ibiryo takes biryoshye. By contrast, a singular noun such as isupu takes iryoshye: "Nteka isupu iryoshye."

messages.content: Ndi ku biro by'umurenge. Ndashaka kubwira umukozi nti: "Ndashaka impapuro yo gusaba icyemezo."
Vuga uti: "Ndashaka impapuro zo gusaba icyemezo." Impapuro ni nyinshi, bityo zijyana na zo, si yo. Nk'umukozi nakubaza nti: "Murashaka gusaba icyemezo ki?"
Nshaka icyemezo bibiri by'amavuko by'abana banjye.
Vuga uti: "Nshaka ibyemezo bibiri by'amavuko by'abana banjye." Icyemezo kimwe gihinduka ibyemezo byinshi. Murakoze kubisobanura; ubu birumvikana ko mushaka ibyemezo bibiri by'amavuko.

“Nimbyuka kare ejo, nzatembera mbere yo kujya ku kazi.” Here, “nimbyuka” introduces the condition, while “nzatembera” gives the future result. “Gutembera” is the natural everyday expression for taking a walk.

messages.content: How can I say, "One farmer plants one tree, but the farmers water the trees"? I want to understand the plural changes.

Say: "Umuhinzi atera igiti kimwe, ariko abahinzi bavomera ibiti." Umuhinzi becomes abahinzi, and igiti becomes ibiti. The verbs also agree: atera has one farmer as its subject, while bavomera has several farmers.
Why do we not simply add an English-style "s"? Also, how can I show whether inka means one cow or several cows?

Kinyarwanda commonly shows number through noun prefixes and agreement rather than adding "s." With inka, the noun itself can look the same: "Inka imwe iri mu rwuri" means one cow is in the pasture, while "Inka nyinshi ziri mu rwuri" means many cows are in the pasture. Imwe or nyinshi and the change from iri to ziri make the number clear.

messages.content: At work I said, "Ejo nzajya kuri meeting." How can I say that fully in Kinyarwanda, and which part shows the future?
Say: "Ejo nzajya mu nama." It means "Tomorrow I will go to the meeting." In nzajya, the future meaning appears in -za-. Compare: "Ubu ngiye mu nama" means "I am going to the meeting now."
How would I say, "Tomorrow we will go to the meeting and prepare the document"?
Say: "Ejo tuzajya mu nama kandi tuzategura inyandiko." The subject changes from "I" to "we," so nzajya becomes tuzajya. The second future verb also begins with tuza-: tuzategura.

messages.content: Soma aka gace: "Aline yanditse inkuru ngufi. Yayisomeye Eric, maze Eric aramwenyura avuga ko inkuru ishimishije. Nyuma, Aline yayihinduye ikinamico." Who wrote the short story?
Aline ni we wanditse inkuru ngufi. The first sentence states this directly: "Aline yanditse inkuru ngufi."
Could I replace ishimishije with irasekeje without changing the meaning?

Oya, si kimwe neza. "Inkuru irashimishije" means the story is enjoyable or pleasing. "Inkuru irasekeje" specifically means the story is funny and makes people laugh. The passage only says that Eric found it enjoyable.
In "Aline yayihinduye ikinamico," what does "it" refer to: the story or the play?
"It" refers to inkuru ngufi, the short story. Aline changed the story into a play, so ikinamico is the result of the change, not the thing represented by -yi- in yayihinduye.

messages.content: Ijambo "inshuti" risobanura iki? Mpa urugero rwerekeye umuryango.
"Inshuti" ni umuntu mufitanye ubucuti. Urugero: "Mushiki wanjye yatumiye inshuti ye ngo dusangire." Aha "inshuti ye" ni umuntu ufitanye ubucuti na mushiki wawe; si ngombwa ko aba uwo mu muryango.
None se iyo nshuti ifashije mushiki wanjye gutegura ameza, nabivuga nte?
Wavuga uti: "Iyo nshuti yafashije mushiki wanjye gutegura ameza." Aha "iyo nshuti" yerekeza kuri ya nshuti mushiki wawe yatumiye; ntitwongeyemo undi muntu.

messages.content: Give me a short Kinyarwanda passage about an everyday sports event. Include the exact time and some singular-plural contrasts, then ask me what happened.

Kamali went at 9:00 a.m., found two balls and six players, and they played for forty minutes. Who won the game, and does the passage say who owned the two balls?

messages.content: How should I translate "I am visiting my aunt today" if I mean that I plan to visit her later today? Please contrast it with a habitual visit.

For the planned visit, say: "Uyu munsi ndajya gusura masenge." Kinyarwanda expresses the intended trip naturally with "ndajya gusura," rather than copying the English form word for word. Contrast: "Nsura masenge buri cyumweru" means "I visit my aunt every week," so that sentence describes a habit.

messages.content: Please help me say, "I planted one bean and two maize plants in the field," and show me the plural of maize plant.
Say: "Nateye igishyimbo kimwe n'ibigori bibiri mu murima." "Ikigori" is one maize plant, while "ibigori" is the plural. The number word agrees with the plural: "bibiri."
Now how do I say, "I watered them"? By "them," I mean everything I just mentioned.
Say: "Navomereye igishyimbo n'ibigori." Repeating both nouns makes it clear that you watered the bean and the two maize plants.
Then how do I say, "They grew well"? This time "they" means only the two maize plants, not the bean.
Say: "Ibigori bibiri byakuze neza." Here "byakuze" refers specifically to "ibigori bibiri," so the bean is not included.

messages.content: I want to say: "The youth group planted three trees beside the river on Saturday." How do I say that in Kinyarwanda?

"Itsinda ry'urubyiruko ryateye ibiti bitatu ku nkombe z'uruzi ku wa Gatandatu." You can also move the time phrase without changing the meaning: "Ku wa Gatandatu, itsinda ry'urubyiruko ryateye ibiti bitatu ku nkombe z'uruzi."
Can I now paraphrase it as "They planted them there on Saturday," with "they" meaning the group and "them" meaning the trees?
Yego: "Ryabiteye aho ku wa Gatandatu." "Rya-" yerekeza ku itsinda, "-bi-" igasimbura ibiti, naho "aho" hakerekeza ku nkombe z'uruzi zavuzwe mbere.
What follow-up question asks why they planted the trees?
Baza uti: "Kuki itsinda ry'urubyiruko ryateye ibyo biti ku nkombe z'uruzi?" Gusubiramo "itsinda ry'urubyiruko" na "ibyo biti" bituma ikibazo gisobanuka neza.
Answer that they planted them to protect the riverbank, but do not say anything about who owns the land.
"Ibyo biti byatewe n'itsinda ry'urubyiruko kugira ngo birinde inkombe z'uruzi." "Bi-" muri "birinde" yerekeza kuri ibyo biti. Interuro ntigira icyo ivuga ku nyir'ubutaka.

messages.content: In "Bisi nshya irahagaze kuri gare," what does irahagaze mean? Which route is the bus taking, and how would the sentence change for several buses?

Irahagaze means the bus is currently stopped or stationary at the station: "Bisi nshya irahagaze kuri gare." The route is not stated, so we cannot identify it. For several buses, say: "Bisi nshya zirahagaze kuri gare." The agreement changes from i- to zi-. By contrast, "Bisi nshya irahagarara kuri gare" can describe a bus that regularly stops there.

messages.content: Give me a short Kinyarwanda passage about taking a bus, then ask me to infer which bus the passenger boarded and why.

He boarded the second bus because the first bus was full. How do I give that answer in Kinyarwanda, and how should I keep the wording around "yari yuzuye" clear?

Say: "Yinjiye muri bisi ya kabiri kuko iya mbere yari yuzuye." Your inference is fully supported by the passage. Keep "yari" and "yuzuye" as two separate words; together, "yari yuzuye" means "was full."

Vuga uti: "Umuturanyi utuye iruhande rwanjye aransuhuza buri gitondo." Dukoresha "utuye" kuko ari umuturanyi usobanurwa.
Nanjye nsuhuza abana batuye muri iyo nzu nimugoroba.
Ni interuro iboneye. Amagambo "batuye muri iyo nzu" agaragaza abana usuhuza nimugoroba.

messages.content: Soma aka gace: "Uyu munsi abaturage bari ku kibuga. Bamwe barategura intebe, abandi barimbisha urubuga." Which actions are happening now?

The actions happening now are "bamwe barategura intebe" and "abandi barimbisha urubuga." The forms "barategura" and "barimbisha" describe what the two groups are doing now. "Abaturage bari ku kibuga" tells us their present location rather than an action they are performing.
Nshaka guhindura umuntu uvugwa. Navuga nte ko umuturanyi umwe ari gutegura intebe?

Vuga uti: "Umuturanyi arategura intebe." Because the subject changes from a group to one person, "barategura" changes to "arategura." Both describe an action happening now; only the agreement changes.

"Nyereka" ni itegeko ritaziguye. Kugira ngo usabe neza, wavuga uti: "Wanyereka aho gare iri?" Iyi mvugo isaba ubufasha mu buryo bworoheje.
Ndabaza umuntu mukuru ntazi. Nakoresha interuro iyihe?
Vuga uti: "Mwanyereka aho gare iri?" Mwanyereka igaragaza icyubahiro iyo ubaza umuntu mukuru cyangwa umuntu mutamenyeranye.

messages.content: Hari umuhanda ibiri ijya kuri gare. Nabigereranya nte?
Banza uvuge uti: "Hari imihanda ibiri ijya kuri gare." "Umuhanda" uhinduka "imihanda" iyo ari myinshi.
Umuhanda wa mbere ni kilometero ebyiri, uwa kabiri ni kilometero enye. Ni uwuhe mugufi?
Umuhanda wa mbere ni wo mugufi: ufite kilometero ebyiri, naho uwa kabiri ufite enye.
Imihanda zombi ziragera kuri gare?
Vuga uti: "Imihanda yombi igera kuri gare?" "Yombi" na "igera" ni byo bijyana na "imihanda."

messages.content: Umuhinzi yavuze ati: "Uyu ni umurima wacu." Sinumva "wacu." Ni uwa nde?
"Umurima wacu" bisobanura ko umurima ari uw'umuvugizi n'abandi bantu, ariko ntituzi abo bandi abo ari bo. In English, "wacu" means "our," while "wanjye" means "my."
Nshaka kumubaza ibijyanye n'amatungo. Navuga nti: "Izi ni inka wawe?"
Vuga uti: "Izi ni inka zawe?" Dukoresha "zawe" kuko "inka" zivugwa ari nyinshi. In English: "Are these your cows?"
